A1.justification: Both PDFs present DynamicTree and contain readable methods, equations, results, figures, and dataset, network, and visualization appendices. Content can be reliably matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original animation and interaction experiments, user-study preferences, timing measurements, and training-strategy and resolution ablations in Section 6.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results for SV4D 2.0 and a user-study comparison with traditional tree animation in Section 6.3.

M1.justification: The sparse voxel spectrum, frequency-conditioned diffusion model, diffusion and LSS losses, two-stage training, mesh-bound Gaussians, and modal interaction procedure remain unchanged, including the appendix architecture parameters.

E1.justification: New Section 6.3 adds evaluation on clean 3D tree models for the traditional-animation comparison, introducing an input scenario distinct from reconstructed real trees. The 8,786-instance training dataset and 13-real-tree evaluation set remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens the comparison methods: SV4D 2.0 joins 4DGen in Figure 3 and Table 1, and Weber and Penn's traditional animation method becomes an evaluated baseline in new Table 2. PhysGaussian and PhysFlow remain the interaction comparators.

E3.justification: The animation preference comparison expands from two methods to three. The new traditional-animation experiment uses clean tree models and the existing perceptual criteria. Training budgets, CLIP metrics, and the four-view interaction evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The training-strategy ablation, resolution sensitivity experiment, and appendix demonstrations of different force directions and magnitudes are retained. The new traditional-method comparison does not include a controlled scanning-noise or robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and preference percentages without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added comparisons introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Substantial comparative results are added: SV4D 2.0 scores 0.0081 CLIP-I and 0.0057 CLIP-T, while new Table 2 reports overall preferences of 57.86% for DynamicTree versus 42.14% for Weber. Table 1 replaces animation preference results, including DynamicTree's 95.7% becoming 94.6% under the expanded comparator set; these are not directly comparable performance measurements. Existing CLIP scores, interaction results, and resolution-ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The spectrum definitions, loss formulas, Gaussian-binding equations, and modal-analysis derivation are unchanged. v2 numbers the previously unnumbered LSS equation and shifts subsequent equation numbers without revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain long-term real-tree animation, sparse voxel spectra for generation and interaction, and the 4DTree dataset. Greater emphasis on structural consistency and physical plausibility restates properties already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 adds a fairness rationale for using clean models and interprets the resulting preferences as evidence of effectiveness and robustness. The voxel-smoothing explanation and limitations concerning global linear motion, deformation artifacts, and limited large-deformation data remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 removes v1's explicit statement that quantitative animation evaluation uses only the input view, without specifying a replacement restriction. This reduces protocol documentation rather than establishing an actual view-selection change. Hardware, hyperparameters, architecture specifications, and appendix data-curation instructions are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds SV4D and SV4D 2.0 and removes Animate124. It retains the same principal research families and positioning around learned 3D motion, physical simulation, and spectral representations.

P1.justification: Several abstract, introduction, and related-work passages are rewritten, and affiliations and citation formatting are updated. Limitations and conclusion become separate subsections in reversed order, and appendix A.1–A.3 becomes A–C. Most methodological and experimental exposition retains its wording and organization.

P2.justification: The paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, moves Figure 1 to the first page, and extensively resizes and relocates figures and tables. Figure 3 and Table 1 gain SV4D 2.0 entries, and a new traditional-animation table is added. Appendix visualizations are retained but redistributed.

improvement.justification: The additional SV4D 2.0 comparison and clean-model comparison with Weber provide broader evidence for the retained comparative claims. The gain is limited: v2 removes the input-view-only evaluation clarification, and the new clean-model results do not directly establish robustness to scanning errors. The method and existing ablation evidence remain unchanged.
